name: Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy 112

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and genetic diagnostic criteria for DEE112

criteria.description: Onset of multiple seizure types (including infantile spasms, tonic-clonic, myoclonic, atonic) in infancy or early childhood
Severe global developmental delay or intellectual disability manifesting in infancy or early childhood
EEG findings of hypsarrhythmia in early infancy, transitioning to multifocal epileptiform discharges
Heterozygous pathogenic variant in GABRB3 identified by molecular genetic testing
Seizures refractory to standard anti-epileptic drugs
Hypotonia in infancy or early childhood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All four major criteria are required for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by identification of a pathogenic GABRB3 variant in a patient with compatible clinical and EEG features.

laboratory: No disease-specific laboratory abnormalities; metabolic workup typically normal
imaging: Brain MRI may show mild cerebral atrophy or be normal
genetic: Heterozygous pathogenic variant in GABRB3 (confirmed by sequencing)
other: EEG: hypsarrhythmia in infancy, evolving to multifocal epileptiform discharges

distinguishingFeatures: GABRA1 mutations; overlapping seizure types but may have later onset
Distinct EEG patterns and response to therapy
GABRG2 mutations; often milder developmental impairment
Different spectrum of seizure types and EEG findings
West syndrome can be secondary to many etiologies, not limited to GABRB3
May lack persistent multifocal discharges and severe ID seen in DEE112

redFlags: Early onset refractory seizures with hypsarrhythmia on EEG
Severe developmental delay in the context of GABRB3 variant
commonPitfalls: Assuming all infantile spasms are due to West syndrome without genetic testing
Missing the diagnosis due to normal brain MRI
Overlooking GABRB3 variants in epilepsy gene panels

extendedDiscriminators.feature: GABRB3-related DEE112 typically presents with more severe developmental delay and earlier onset
DEE112 has a confirmed GABRB3 pathogenic variant and persistent multifocal discharges beyond infancy
DEE112 often shows more severe intellectual disability and less favorable seizure control

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of pathogenic GABRB3 variant on genetic testing
Normal development prior to seizure onset
